name: Adam Juma Haruun
title: Crop Disease Identification System Using Convolutional Neural Networks
description: This project report presents the design, evaluation and implementation of Crop Disease Identifier System using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), to address the challenge of crop diseases affecting agricultural productivity, particularly in South Sudan, with a focus on tomato and watermelon crops that are highly susceptible to diseases reducing yield and threatening food security. It identifies key gaps in traditional detection methods, including delayed diagnosis, limited access to agricultural experts, and lack of affordable technological solutions for smallholder farmers, and addresses these challenges by developing an intelligent system based on a MobileNet CNN model with transfer learning implemented in Python using TensorFlow, following an agile methodology that includes data collection, preprocessing, augmentation, model training, validation, where the trained model achieved an overall classification accuracy of 96.81%, with training accuracy exceeding 97% and validation accuracy above 96%, alongside high precision (96.5%), recall(96.2%), and F1-score (96.3%), demonstrating reliable and balanced predictive performance across disease classes, while loss curves indicated minimal overfitting due to effective data augmentation and transfer learning; the results confirm that the proposed system is efficient, accurate, and suitable for real-time deployment, enabling rapid and accessible disease diagnosis for farmers, and the study concludes that integrating artificial intelligence into agriculture can significantly improve early disease detection, enhance crop management, and support sustainable agricultural practices, although limitations such as restricted dataset diversity and limited crop coverage highlight the need for further research and system expansion.

name: Agar Marial Riak
title: Design and Implementation of Smart Malaria Diagnosis Assistant in Rural Clinics
description: Malaria remains a significant global health challenge, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa where healthcare systems are constrained by limited infrastructure and skilled personnel. According to the World Health Organization, approximately 249 million malaria cases and over 608,000 deaths were reported globally in 2023, with the majority occurring in Africa [1]. In South Sudan, limited access to reliable diagnostic services, especially in rural areas, contributes to delayed diagnosis and increased mortality. Conventional diagnostic methods, including microscopy and Rapid Diagnostic Tests (RDTs), are widely used but present several limitations. Microscopy requires trained personnel and controlled laboratory conditions, while RDTs may produce inconsistent results due to environmental and sensitivity constraints. These challenges necessitate the development of more efficient and accurate diagnostic solutions. This study presents the design and implementation of a Smart Malaria Diagnosis Assistant (SMDA), an artificial intelligence-based system that automates malaria detection using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). The model was trained and evaluated using the publicly available Kaggle Malaria Cell Images dataset [3]. The system is deployed through a Flask-based web application integrated with a MySQL database, enabling real-time image upload, automated classification, and storage of diagnostic results. The system is designed to operate effectively in low-resource environments with support for mobile-based image capture. Performance evaluation using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score demonstrates that the proposed system achieves high diagnostic accuracy while significantly reducing detection time.

name: Awut Deng Aquer
title: Securing Harvest: Automated Detection and Classification of Rice Diseases Using DCNN
description: To support South Sudan's goal of achieving rice self-sufficiency, this study addresses the critical challenge of endemic rice leaf diseases that cause severe crop failure across major agricultural regions like the Aweil scheme. Recognizing that traditional manual visual inspection is slow, subjective, and often identifies diseases too late, the thesis proposes a deep learning approach using a ResNet-50 Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) architecture. By leveraging residual learning and skip connections for deep feature extraction, the model achieved high classification performance with an F1-score exceeding 0.90 across healthy and diseased leaf images. The study confirms the strong potential of residual networks as scalable tools for early disease detection, offering a foundation for future mobile deployment to support farmers, agricultural extension workers, and national food security.

name: Ayath Agany
title: Deep Learning- Based Automated for Real-Time Heart Attack (Myocardial Infraction) Screening
description: Heart attacks, or myocardial infarctions (MI), remain a leading cause of global mortality, necessitating urgent advancements in early and accurate detection. Traditional diagnostic methods often suffer from delayed results and a reliance on expert manual analysis, which can be prone to human error. This research proposes an automated, real-time Heart Attack Screening System utilizing Deep Learning (DL) architectures to facilitate early intervention. The methodology focuses on processing structured clinical features such as age, cholesterol, and heart rate. The system employs a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) architecture to effectively capture non-linear relationships between risk factors. The model achieved a high test accuracy of 93.27%. The final system serves as a robust, accessible tool for healthcare providers, potentially reducing mortality rates through rapid, data-driven diagnostic support in both clinical and low-resource settings. The study recommends integrating this tool into local clinic triage systems to prioritize high-risk patients. The developed model performs a three-category categorical classification, mapping predictions into Low Risk (0), Moderate Risk (1), and High Risk (2), ensuring a more clinically meaningful risk stratification compared to binary approaches.

name: Biet Puoric Matuong
title: Smart Irrigation System
description: This research presents the design and implementation of a smart irrigation system using Freedom Farm in Luri Central Equatoria State, South Sudan, as a case study. Agriculture in South Sudan is predominantly dependent on rainfall and manual irrigation practices, which are often inefficient, labor-intensive and prone to water wastage. At Luri Freedom Farm, irrigation is largely conducted using traditional methods without real-time monitoring of soil and environmental conditions, leading to inconsistent crop yields and inefficient water utilization. The proposed system integrates soil moisture sensors, temperature and humidity sensors, Internet of Things (IoT)-based communication, and automated control mechanisms to optimize irrigation scheduling. The system is designed to operate under resource-constrained conditions, including unreliable electricity and limited connectivity, by incorporating low-cost components and solar-powered energy solutions. A prototype of the smart irrigation system was developed and deployed at Luri Freedom Farm to monitor environmental parameters and automate irrigation processes. Data were collected under two conditions: traditional irrigation and smart irrigation. The performance of the system was evaluated based on water consumption, crop yield, system reliability and cost effectiveness. The findings indicate that the proposed system significantly reduces water usage by approximately 30–40% while improving crop productivity and reducing manual labor. This study contributes to the development of sustainable agricultural practices and provides a scalable solution for improving irrigation efficiency in South Sudan and other resource constrained regions.

name: Emmanuel Deng Mei
title: Lightweight Deep Learning Architecture for Realtime Crop Pest Detection
description: This study addresses the critical challenge of real-time crop pest detection in resource-constrained agricultural environments, where invasive pests contribute to over 40% of global crop losses and cause significant economic damage to smallholder farmers. To mitigate these losses, this research proposes a Lightweight Deep Learning Architecture (LDLA) that integrates an Efficient Spatial Attention (ESA) mechanism into a MobileNetV2 framework. This hybrid approach aims to enhance categorical classification across eight high-impact pest classes by focusing the model's receptive field on relevant biological features while maintaining a low computational footprint suitable for mobile devices. Utilizing an applied research design process, the study leveraged the large-scale IP102 dataset to train and validate the proposed architecture. To ensure edge-device feasibility, the model was subjected to rigorous optimization techniques, including Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) and structured pruning, specifically aimed at reducing inference latency for real-world deployment. Experimental results indicate that while the model achieved a robust training accuracy of 86.6%, the final validation accuracy reached 69.1%. Although this performance fell below the initial 85% benchmark, the study provides critical insights into the inherent complexities of the IP102 dataset, which is characterized by high inter-class similarity and diverse environmental backgrounds that mimic actual field conditions. The successful integration of Efficient Spatial Attention significantly improved the model's feature extraction capabilities; however, the performance gap suggests that additional data balancing and class-specific augmentation are required to overcome environmental noise. This research establishes a vital technical baseline for deploying lightweight, attention-aware diagnostic tools in digital agriculture, offering a scalable path toward more resilient and automated crop protection strategies.

name: Kuot Chol Majok
title: Automated Waste Classification for Recycling in Juba City Using Lightweight Deep Convolutional Neural Networks
description: Waste management has emerged as a crucial global challenge, driven by rapid urbanization and projected annual global waste generation set to surge from 2.1 billion tons in 2023 to 3.4 billion tons by 2050. This exponential increase necessitates a shift away from inefficient manual processes toward automated, intelligent systems. In Juba City, South Sudan, the total reliance on manual labor for waste collection has led to a collapse in municipal services, resulting in widespread open dumping, environmental contamination, and severe occupational health risks (15-20% injury risk) for workers handling sharps and hazardous materials. Critically, the poor classification and mixing of collected waste entirely suppresses resource recovery, intensifying the scarcity of valuable materials needed in the region. The objective is to develop a novel, automated solution leveraging Artificial Intelligence (AI) for real-time waste detection and classification into high-priority categories (e.g., biodegradable, paper, plastic, metal, cardboard, shoes, clothes, brown glass, green glass, white glass, trash and paper) to enable efficient recycling and proper disposal. The methodology employs the state-of-the-art MobileNetV2 (A lightweight CNN architecture) deep learning framework, selected for its superior speed and accuracy trade-off, optimized via transfer learning and aggressive data augmentation on aggregated datasets (Kaggle benchmarks, local images) to ensure robustness against environmental clutter. The Simulated results demonstrate high performance metrics, including an average Precision of 92% and an F1-Score of 91%, establishing the technical feasibility of automating waste classification to minimize contamination, enhance worker safety, and transform waste management in Juba City into a viable, resource-generating opportunity, thereby supporting a cleaner and more sustainable future.

name: Lioto Samuel Simon
title: Design and Implementation of a Network Intrusion Detection System Using Machine Learning
description: This study presents the design and implementation of a Machine Learning-based Network Intrusion Detection System (NIDS) for multi-class classification, intended for better detection of various types of cyber-attacks in contemporary network environments. The proposed NIDS was created using the CICIDS2017 dataset and classifies network traffic into four classes: Benign, DoS/DDoS, Brute Force, and PortScan. To ensure better quality and effectiveness of the data and proposed model, various preprocessing techniques were used, including data cleaning, normalization, and encoding. Furthermore, to resolve the problem of class imbalance in network intrusion detection, this study used the Synthetic Minority Over-sampling Technique (SMOTE), which increases the number of minority classes in network attack detection. The results obtained in this study indicate that the proposed model was able to achieve an overall classification accuracy of around 99.28%, demonstrating better discrimination between different types of network traffic. However, it was also found that certain classes had lower precision due to overlapping features and synthetic data generation. These results highlight the need for evaluating intrusion detection systems with precise per-class performance measures like precision, recall, and F1-score, rather than accuracy. The research concludes that machine learning techniques are highly effective for solving multi-class intrusion detection problems, but the need for further optimization to minimize false positives and improve the detection of less common types of attacks remains, thereby improving the reliability of the intrusion detection system.

name: Malual Majur Dhaal & Benis Garang Wantok
title: School of Computer Science and Information Technology E-Learning Platform
description:
The study investigated the use of E-learning platforms and student satisfaction in the School
of Computer Science and Information Technology at the University of Juba. It aims to examine
how E-learning components peroxided by internet security, internet efficiency, and internet
reliability affect student satisfaction within the institution. The study adopted a survey research
design, and a simple random sampling method was used to select students who are familiar
with E-learning platforms in the School of Computer Science and Information Technology.
The data collected for the study comprised primary data obtained through the administration
of questionnaires. A multiple regression method was employed for data analysis. The findings
reveal that the coefficient of internet reliability is significant and positive, indicating that
internet reliability has a strong impact on student satisfaction with E-learning platforms. This
implies that reliable internet access is a key determinant of students’ satisfaction in E-learning
environments. The study concludes that internet reliability, internet efficiency, and internet
security all have significant impacts on student satisfaction with E-learning platforms in the
School of Computer Science and Information Technology at the University of Juba. However,
students place greater emphasis on internet reliability particularly in terms of accessing
learning materials and completing academic tasks than on security or efficiency.

name: Nesnea Khadi Silvano
title: Deep Learning Decision Support System for Automated Diabetic Retinopathy Screening and Grading
description: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) stands as the most prevalent diabetic eye ailment and constitutes one of the primary causes of blindness worldwide. Detecting and classifying retinal images can be laborious and demands specialized expertise. The proposed method employs the MobileNetV2 architecture, a lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) optimized for mobile and edge deployment. Using Transfer Learning on the ImageNet dataset, the model was fine-tuned to classify retinal fundus images into the five International Clinical Diabetic Retinopathy (ICDR) stages: Normal, Mild, Moderate, Severe, and Proliferative DR. To ensure robustness, data preprocessing techniques including normalization, resizing to 224 × 224 pixels, and data augmentation were applied to mitigate class imbalance. To enhance the resilience of the models and mitigate overfitting issues, data augmentation approaches were implemented. The network underwent two levels of training. The initial level involved a feature extraction network with a customized classifier head, followed by fine-tuning the resulting network from the previous step through the unfreezing of certain layers. The efficacy of the proposed strategy was assessed through qualitative and quantitative evaluations using Kaggle’s diabetic retinopathy detection dataset. Experimental results demonstrate that the model achieved an accuracy of 74% on the testing dataset. Notably, the method exhibited high reliability in "No-DR" screening, achieving an 83% precision for Class 0, which is essential for reducing unnecessary referrals. With an average inference latency of 3.1 seconds, the system is capable of providing real-time diagnostic support. The findings suggest that this approach offers a scalable, cost-effective solution for task-shifting in primary healthcare centers, enabling general health workers to identify at-risk patients early and preserve sight in underserved populations.

name: Emmanuel Khamis Victor
title: Spatiotemporal Abnormal Behavior Detection Model Using ResNet50-LSTM
description: The rapid expansion of surveillance systems in public and private environments has created a strong demand for intelligent technologies capable of automatically detecting abnormal or violent activities. Although modern surveillance cameras capture large volumes of video data, accurately interpreting human behavior in complex real-world environments remains a significant challenge due to factors such as illumination variations, motion blur, occlusion, and crowded scenes. Traditional frame-based detection methods often fail to capture temporal motion patterns and therefore generate false alarms when harmless activities such as running or sudden crowd movement occur. To address these limitations, this research proposes a deep learning model for abnormal behavior detection  based on a hybrid deep learning architecture that combines ResNet50 and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks for spatiotemporal analysis. The CNN component utilizes a pre-trained ResNet50 model to extract high-level spatial features from individual video frames, while the LSTM network captures temporal dependencies across frame sequences to identify patterns associated with violent behavior. The model was trained and evaluated using the RWF-2000 dataset, a real-world surveillance dataset containing videos categorized as violent and non-violent activities. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed ResNet50–LSTM architecture effectively distinguishes violent interactions from normal activities by analyzing both spatial appearance and temporal motion patterns. The performance of the model was evaluated using accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score, demonstrating strong classification capability and reduced false alarm rates compared to traditional frame-level approaches. On the RWF-2000 dataset [7], the model achieved a test accuracy of 72.5%. The model performs binary classification, where “Non-Fight” is mapped to Class 1 and “Fight” is mapped to Class 0. These results highlight the effectiveness of spatiotemporal deep learning techniques for automated surveillance, showing potential to improve the reliability of abnormal behavior detection in real-world environments.

name: Ngor Wek Wek
title: Automatic Wildlife Monitoring System
description: The conservation of wildlife depends on precise observations of species populations, habitats, and behaviors. Wildlife monitoring is a critical component of biodiversity conservation and ecological research. Effective wildlife detection systems help track animal populations, study their behavior, and protect their habitats. Traditional techniques like manual surveys and camera trap analysis are labor-intensive, time-consuming, and error-prone. To automatically recognize and categorize animal species, this paper suggests an automated wildlife monitoring utilizing image recognition and Machine learning. The system achieves strong recognition under a number of environmental conditions by utilizing preprocessing techniques (noise reduction, image enhancement, and feature extraction) along with deep learning techniques like CNNs. In relation to conventional methods, the framework greatly increases speed, scalability, and accuracy by enabling real-time detection, tracking, and biodiversity pattern analysis. The paper illustrates how artificial intelligence can transform ecological research by providing dependable and automated methods for protecting biodiversity.

name: Deng Deng Madut
title: Automated Data Breach Notification System (A Case Study of Zain South Sudan)
description: This research presents the design and implementation of an Automated Data Breach Notification System (ADBNS), a web-based cybersecurity solution developed to reduce the notification delays following data breaches in South Sudan. Traditional notification methods are manual and inefficient, often exposing users to further risks. The proposed system utilizes a three-tier architecture consisting of a Bootstrap-based frontend, a PHP backend, and a MySQL database. It enables administrators to upload breach logs and automatically notify affected users via email using SMTP protocols. The system was deployed on the Infinity Free cloud platform using the InnoDB storage engine to ensure relational integrity. Results from threat simulations demonstrate that the ADBNS can identify a breach and generate an audit record in the notifications table in less than 3 seconds. The study concludes that such automated frameworks are essential for local institutions to comply with emerging digital privacy standards and to protect citizens from secondary identity theft. This system addresses the critical delay in notifying users after a data compromise. The Automated Data Breach Notification System was designed to bridge this gap using a web-based architecture. Testing revealed a 100% accuracy rate in matching records with a processing time of less than 4 seconds for mid-sized datasets. This study concludes that automation is essential for modern cybersecurity compliance and user protection.
